title: fix(plugin-security): the seed ownership hand-over yields to the event loop between 50-row batches, so a sign-in during it is answered
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-project-manager"} -->
_Requested by **Leehom** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X?thread=cmsg_01TenzsRopZj4jMbvjX8uz1X9mRXg8QNKdP2mmSLvmtm2L)_

Fixes #26825

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:种子落定后把种子数据移交给平台管理员的那一步(`claimSeedOwnership`,以及多组织版 `claimOrgSeedOwnership`)改为每批 50 行写入,每写一批让出一次事件循环;按行写的路径每 50 行让出一次。
- **为什么改**:实测在 `os serve --dev`(文件型 sqlite,1,500 行带种子文件的种子)上,这一步是一次覆盖 1,500 行的写入,耗时 2,641 ms,整个事件循环被占住约 2.7 秒,期间的登录请求要等 2.0–2.9 秒;改后最长卡顿 190 ms,同期登录 p50 317 ms、最慢 539 ms。
- **风险与回滚**:成功路径结果不变(同样的行、同样的所有者、每行一条审计行)。唯一变化在失败时:一个 5,000 行分块里只有部分批次被拒时,其余批次已归属、剩下的行由下一次认领补上(以前整块都不归属);整块全被拒时与原来完全相同。席位已接受此差异。回滚即撤销本 PR。
- **先看**:`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/claim-seed-ownership.ts`(`claimPredicateInBatches`、`CLAIM_HANDOVER_ROWS`、`claimRows` 里的让出);`packages/plugins/organizations/src/claim-org-seed-ownership.ts`(`claimChunk`);两个新的 `*-yield.pin.test.ts`。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run src/claim-seed-ownership-yield.pin.test.ts`,预期 5 passed。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

**The reading first, on `main` at `e78d7057`.** The card's attribution came from a CPU profile whose async stacks are partial, so it was re-measured before any edit. A scratch app (one object with a file field, 1,500 seeded rows, each with a 20 KB `seedFile`) booted with `os serve --dev` over file-backed sqlite, `OS_INLINE_SEED_BUDGET_MS=1` so the seed settles in the background, a 20 ms event-loop lag sampler preloaded, and a sign-in (`POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in/email`) every 250 ms:

- Three boots: the event loop stalled 2,763 / 2,762 / 2,742 ms in one stretch that starts at `Seed loading complete` and ends at `handed 1500 seeded record(s)`. Sign-ins issued inside it took 2.0–3.2 s.
- A timing marker spliced into `plugin-security`'s `dist` around the claim's `ql.update` (removed afterwards; the dist was copied back) read three writes: `usr_system` arm 2 ms, the NULL arm's ONE write over 1,500 ids **2,641 ms**, then the warm re-pass 2 ms. So the whole stall is one engine write.
- The CPU profile of that stretch is per-row hook work inside that write: better-sqlite3 `_query`/`prepare`, plugin-audit's `writeAudit` → `persistAuditTrailRow` (one audit row per row), engine `insert`, the storage file-reference hooks, plugin-auth and plugin-sharing middleware. Control on the same boot without a file field: the claim ran about 1.1 s with no single stall above 483 ms.

**Why the cure is a smaller write, not a yield inside one.** The engine runs a predicate write and its after-hooks in one transaction (`inAfterAbortUnit`), and SQLite's pool holds one connection. A yield inside the write would leave the sign-in waiting on the pool instead of the event loop. So the atomic unit has to shrink.

**The fix.**

1. `claim-seed-ownership.ts`: the NULL arm's chunk (still `CLAIM_PAGE_ROWS` = 5,000 ids, the unit of failure reporting) is written `CLAIM_HANDOVER_ROWS` = 50 ids at a time by the new `claimPredicateInBatches`, with one `setImmediate` turn after every write. 50 is measured: about 1.8 ms of hook work per claimed row, so about 90 ms per batch. The `owner_id = usr_system` arm is unchanged (one predicate write, paged only on the per-row hook refusal) and yields after it. The by-row path (`claimRows`, objects whose stored expression reads `owner_id`) yields after every 50 rows; its writes were already one per row.
2. `claim-org-seed-ownership.ts` (the multi-organization twin) had the same unbroken run: one write per 5,000-id chunk, inside the request that creates the organization. `claimChunk` now writes 50 ids at a time with a yield after each, and `claimChunkByRow` yields every 50 rows.
3. The yield helper is a module-private copy in each file, by the seat's ruling on this card (option B): the existing copies in `metadata-protocol/src/seed-files.ts` and `core/src/utils/import-runner.ts` are not exported, and exporting one would widen a published surface. Each docblock names the other copies.

**Failure semantics, as accepted by the seat.** Success is unchanged: the same rows, the same owner, one audit row per claimed row. A chunk every batch of which is refused behaves exactly as on `main`: plugin-security rethrows the first refusal so the caller logs the same single warning and the chunk stays unowned; organizations logs the same `the N seeded row(s) of this write stay owner-less` warning. When only some batches of a chunk are refused, the accepted batches stay owned, one warning names the rows left unowned (count, the first 20 ids, the first error), and the next run claims them; on `main` one refused write left the whole chunk unowned.

**Wall time.** The hand-over itself is not faster: on the live boot it spanned 3.4 s after the fix against 2.6 s before, because sign-ins now run between its batches.

## Why

The first admin who signs in while a demo or package seed is still settling waited several seconds on a fresh boot.

## Tests

- New `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/claim-seed-ownership-yield.pin.test.ts`, on a real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3 `:memory:`), 320 seeded rows, a code-registered `afterUpdate` hook writing one audit row per updated row (the shape of plugin-audit's writer) and a `beforeUpdate` hook that can refuse named rows:
  - `re-owns at most one batch of rows between two macrotask turns`
  - `serves a read issued during the hand-over before the hand-over ends`
  - `hands every seeded row to the admin with one audit row per claimed row`
  - `a refused batch leaves only its rows unowned, says which, and the next run claims them`
  - `every batch refused: nothing claimed, and the one warning a refused chunk always gave`
- New `packages/plugins/organizations/src/claim-org-seed-ownership-yield.pin.test.ts`: the same five on `SqliteWasmDriver`, plus a row in another organization that stays untouched.
- Updated shape pins that counted writes per 5,000-id chunk: plugin-security `issues ONE predicate write per unowned shape and hand-over batch`, the over-ceiling pin (the NULL arm's writes counted apart from the `usr_system` arm's), `writes the seeded ids in hand-over batches`; organizations' 10,500-row pin, the unreadable-count pin (now one warning per chunk) and the failed-chunk pin (now refuses every write of the second chunk).

**Red first.** Production source restored to `main` (`git show e78d7057:FILE`), the new pins run, restored from `HEAD` and proven by blob hash:

- plugin-security: 3 failed, 2 passed. `no macrotask turn ran while the hand-over ran: expected 1 to be greater than 6.4`; `expected [ 'hand-over', 'read' ] to deeply equal [ 'read', 'hand-over' ]`; the partial-failure pin red (`main` leaves the whole chunk unowned). The result pin and the every-batch-refused pin are GREEN on `main`: that is the proof that ownership, audit rows and the total-failure warning are identical.
- organizations: the same 3 failed, 2 passed.

**Ablations** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor counts and the HEAD-blob restore checked by the tool; the tests import source, so no `dist` is involved):

- A, the yield resolves at once: plugin-security 2 failed (the two yield pins); organizations 2 failed (the same two).
- B, `CLAIM_HANDOVER_ROWS = CLAIM_PAGE_ROWS`: plugin-security 3 failed (`expected 5 to be greater than 6.4`, `expected 320 to be less than 320`, partial-failure pin).
- C, no rethrow when every batch is refused: plugin-security 1 failed (the every-batch-refused pin's warning text).

**Live re-measure** with the fix built into `dist`, same app and boot: the stretch from `Seed loading complete` to `handed 1500` had no stall above 190 ms (before: 2,669–2,763 ms in one stretch), and the 14 sign-ins issued in it answered p50 317 ms, slowest 539 ms (before: p50 1,967 ms, slowest 2,698 ms).

## Acceptance notes

- **Sharing rules on a large seeded object.** plugin-sharing's `afterUpdate` recomputes per row up to 1,000 rows per write and above that revokes the object's rule grants and re-grants them in the background (with a warning). A 50-row batch is always under that cap, so on an object with sharing rules and more than 1,000 seeded rows the claim now recomputes per row inline (no revoke-and-re-grant window) instead of one revoke plus a queued re-grant. The end state is the same rule grants; the `CLAIM_PAGE_ROWS` docblock reasoning about the 1,000 cap still applies to the `usr_system` arm's pages.
- **The `usr_system` arm is unchanged**, by ruling. It is still one predicate write over every such row, so a seed whose records set `owner_id` to the seed identity would still be claimed in one run. No producer was found: HotCRM and the examples write no `owner_id` in seeds, and the measured seed landed every row NULL. Noted, not filed.
- On `InMemoryDriver` the NULL arm's cost does not change: an `id IN` list of B ids over T rows costs T×B per write and there are N/B writes, the same T×N as one write.
